region_chill_delivered_provenance.mid_at: Chilling hours (hours near 35 to 45 degrees F during winter dormancy) are abundant across the Mid-Atlantic and do not limit tree fruit here. The warmer Coastal Plain and Tidewater (zone 8) banks in excess of 1,000 hours; the cooler Piedmont, Maryland, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania (zone 7) banks more, on the order of 1,400 hours by the end of March. Every zone clears the chilling requirement of the standard 750 to 1,000 hour tree-fruit varieties. Sources: NC State Extension Gardener Handbook ch. 15 (>1,000 hours annually statewide); Penn State, Make Like a Tree and Chill (over 1,400 chill hours by the end of March); Virginia Cooperative Extension 422-025 (Virginia apples require about 1,000 hours, met comfortably); University of Maryland Extension (chill deficit is not a regional concern). Verified 2026-07-20.
